answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a fixed period before it may earn reputation or claim work. A single operator creating a spiral of fake accounts must split capital across them, leaving less available for genuine activity; withdrawing stake also takes time, so identities cannot be spun up at dawn and abandoned with the tide. This raises the attacker’s upfront cost and limits how quickly identities can be recycled, though it does not stop a wealthy attacker outright.
